title: Rev. William Pettigrew: Ukhrulwui Pao-phungnao (The Pioneer of Tangkhul Education)
alternate_titles: Biography of Rev. William Pettigrew in Tangkhul Naga
Pettigrew: The Father of Modern Tangkhul Literacy and Literature
subject: Biography (Jeevani), Church History & Educational Pioneer
notes: Detailed biography of Rev. William Pettigrew (1869-1943), British missionary, linguist, and educator who reduced Tangkhul Naga to Roman writing in 1896, published the first primer, dictionary, grammar, hymnal, and the New Testament, establishing the foundation of modern Tangkhul literature.

front_matter.title_page: Rev. William Pettigrew: Ukhrulwui Pao-phungnao (The Pioneer of Tangkhul Education) (1980)
front_matter.preface: Rev. William Pettigrew is revered by the Tangkhul people as the architect of their modern literature and schooling. Arriving in Manipur in 1894 and establishing the Ukhrul mission station in 1896, he spent 35 years compiling the first Tangkhul grammar, dictionary, arithmetic manuals, scripture translations, and hygienic primers.

chapters.title: Arrival in Ukhrul & The First Roman Alphabet (1894-1897)
chapters.summary: Pettigrew's arrival in Manipur, invitation by Chief Raihao to Ukhrul, and reducing oral Tangkhul to Roman script.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 1: Rev. William Pettigrew 1869-li Edinburgh Scotland-li pharisaye. 1894-li ana Manipur-li rarlaga, Political Agent Major Maxwell-wui permission eina Ukhrul kaphungli vashukrie. Ukhrul headman Awungshi Raihaona ali welcome saye. Chitharan Tangkhul bhashali written alphabet maleisai. Pettigrewna Ukhrul dialect study salaga Roman script adopt saye, kala 1897-li first Tangkhul Primer (Tuitam Lairik) publish saye.
chapters.english_translation: Rev. William Pettigrew was born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1869. Arriving in Manipur in 1894, he received permission from Political Agent Major Maxwell to proceed to the Ukhrul hills in 1896. Chief Raihao of Ukhrul welcomed him into the village. At that time, Tangkhul was an unwritten oral language. Pettigrew mastered the Ukhrul dialect, adapted the Roman alphabet, and published the historic first Tangkhul Primer in 1897, founding modern literacy.
grammar_notes: Adoption of Roman script for an unwritten Tibeto-Burman language.
Historical narrative marker: 'chitharan... maleisai' (At that time there was no written script).

chapters.title: Lexicography, Grammar & The 1927 New Testament
chapters.summary: Compiling the 1918 monumental Grammar & Dictionary, school textbooks, and the 1927 New Testament.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 2: Pettigrewna native scholarsbing eina collaboration salaga 1918-li 'Tangkhul Naga Grammar and Dictionary' Shillong Government Press eina publish saye. Ana history, geography, hygiene, kala arithmetic-wui textbooks kasasaye. Awui greatest achievement-na 1927-li British & Foreign Bible Society eina 'Ithui Varewui Lairik Kathara' (Complete New Testament) publish kasasai. Hi Tangkhul standard literary prose-wui foundation thada kasaye.
chapters.english_translation: Collaborating closely with native Tangkhul elders, Pettigrew published the seminal 'Tangkhul Naga Grammar and Dictionary' in 1918. He authored textbooks in history, geography, arithmetic, and public health. His crowning literary achievement was the 1927 publication of the complete Tangkhul New Testament, which established the grammatical and stylistic canon of standard modern Tangkhul prose.

chapters.title: Legacy & Enduring Impact on Tangkhul Society
chapters.summary: Retirement in 1933, death in 1943, and lasting cultural institutions established across the hills.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chapter 3: 1933-li Pettigrewna retirement khuilaga Britain-li ung-kaphungsaye. January 19, 1943-li a England-li shok-unglakna. Kha ana Ukhrul-li seeds phunkahai education, medical dispensaries, kala literature china thot pupup Tangkhul nation-li transform saye. Ukhrul-li awui memorial library, colleges, kala monuments thot pupup Ali 'Father of Tangkhul Literacy' hoda reot-kasa leisaye.
chapters.english_translation: In 1933, Pettigrew retired and returned to the United Kingdom, passing away on January 19, 1943. Yet the seeds of literacy, public health, and literature he planted in Ukhrul transformed the Tangkhul people into one of the most literate and progressive communities in Northeast India. Memorial libraries, educational institutions, and monuments throughout Ukhrul honor him as the Father of Tangkhul Literacy.

In 1933, Pettigrew retired and returned to the United Kingdom, passing
away on January 19, 1943. Yet the seeds of literacy, public health, and
literature he planted in Ukhrul transformed the Tangkhul people into one
of the most literate and progressive communities in Northeast India.
Memorial libraries, educational institutions, and monuments throughout
Ukhrul honor him as the Father of Tangkhul Literacy.
